title: Discern: The Unimportance of Practically Everything
coreMove: Rank options sharply enough to release good-looking noise before it dilutes the contribution that matters.
sourcePressure: The chapter applies the law of the vital few to show that almost everything is noise and only a small number of options deserve concentrated effort.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would say everything is important in different ways and ask the reader to balance it all.

exampleSpecs.domain: museum conservation lab after a roof leak exposes a backlog
exampleSpecs.audience: conservator surrounded by many damaged objects
exampleSpecs.stakes: equal care for every item would lose the most historically fragile works
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She sorts the wet inventory by irreversible loss risk and moves two ceremonial textiles ahead of popular display pieces.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A damp inventory clipboard rests on blotting paper.

exampleSpecs.domain: minor-league pitching coach reviewing twenty bullpen metrics
exampleSpecs.stakes: fixing all stats evenly will miss the vital mechanical cause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He predicts velocity matters, then overlays walk clusters and finds one release-point drift driving most losses.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A bullpen chart is marked with red walk clusters.

exampleSpecs.domain: disaster-relief warehouse sorting donated supplies after a flood
exampleSpecs.audience: relief coordinator sorting mountains of good intentions
exampleSpecs.stakes: time spent on low-utility donations delays what victims actually need
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She marks the pallet tags by immediate shelter value and sends costume boxes to later sorting.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Pallet tags hang from wet cardboard towers.

exampleSpecs.domain: indie game studio reading thousands of beta-test comments
exampleSpecs.audience: studio lead with too much feedback
exampleSpecs.stakes: popular comments can distract from the few defects killing retention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before, every comment gets a label; after, he ranks only patterns tied to day-two quit data.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A feedback spreadsheet sits beside a retention graph.

exampleSpecs.domain: community health researcher allocating a mobile screening van
exampleSpecs.audience: researcher choosing between many plausible stops
exampleSpecs.stakes: equal distribution may miss the few neighborhoods carrying most risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She points to the incidence map and moves the van from the vocal district to the untreated cluster.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An incidence map is folded over a van schedule.

exampleSpecs.domain: luthier choosing repairs for a school orchestra’s donated instruments
exampleSpecs.stakes: repairing visible damage first may not restore playable section balance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He lines up cracked bridges and warped pegs, then repairs the four instruments that unlock a full cello section.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Cracked bridges sit beside a section roster.
